name: Nanoleaf Essentials A19 (Matter, US)

radios.note: Thread for Matter control; Bluetooth for setup and direct control from the Nanoleaf app.

matter.note: CSA certificate CSA22099MAT40099-24 (Nanoleaf Essentials A19/A60), certified 2022-11-14, Thread and Bluetooth transport.

apple_home.note: Via Matter over Thread; needs a Thread border router such as a HomePod mini, HomePod (2nd gen) or Apple TV 4K.

google_home.note: Via Matter over Thread; needs a Thread border router such as a Nest Hub (2nd gen), Nest Hub Max or Nest Wifi Pro.

alexa.note: Nanoleaf's SKU page lists Alexa; Amazon supports Matter-over-Thread lights on Echo devices. Needs an Echo or eero that is a Thread border router. Nanoleaf's older FAQ still says Alexa is 'coming soon'.

smartthings.note: Nanoleaf lists SmartThings; works via Matter over Thread with a SmartThings hub that is a Thread border router.

home_assistant.note: Via the official Matter integration; Thread devices need a Thread border router.

hubRequired.note: Nanoleaf says the bulb can be set up and controlled over Bluetooth in the Nanoleaf app with no hub. Matter and ecosystem control need a Thread border router.

localControl.note: Matter runs over the local network (Thread/IPv6), and Bluetooth app control is direct.

colorType.note: Over 16 million colours plus tunable white (2700–6500 K).

lumens.note: Nanoleaf's SKU page gives 806 lm average and 1100 lm max, and rates the bulb as a 60 W equivalent, which matches 806 lm, so we use 806. Its US 3-pack page says 900 lm average / 1000 lm max.

summary: Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, SmartThings and Home Assistant all control the Nanoleaf Essentials A19 (NF080B03-1A19E) as a Matter light, once a Thread border router such as a HomePod mini or Nest Hub (2nd gen) is on your network. Without one, the Nanoleaf app still runs it directly over Bluetooth. It's a full-colour E26 bulb with tunable white from 2700 to 6500 K. Nanoleaf rates it at 806 lumens average, a 60 W equivalent, and 1100 lumens at maximum.
caveats: Ecosystem control needs a Thread border router, such as a HomePod mini, Nest Hub (2nd gen), or a Thread-capable Echo or eero.
Nanoleaf's brightness figures vary: 806 lm average and 1100 lm max on the SKU page, 900 lm average and 1000 lm max on its US 3-pack page.
Nanoleaf's older FAQ still calls Alexa support 'coming soon', though the current product page lists it.
